notes: NIAH rating: National. Freestanding timber-and-wrought-iron glasshouse erected in 1884, comprising a triple-height central house with a domed lantern, curved roof wings, and a substantial glazed range. The NIAH describes a complex iron-and-timber framework, cast-iron columns and walkways, historic glazing patterns, ventilation winch system and original heating infrastructure. The structure was prefabricated by James Boyd in Paisley and erected in Dublin in nine months. A nationally rated landmark of Victorian engineering and horticultural architecture within the gardens established in 1795. Its scale, ironwork, glazing and faithful conservation make it a major component of the historic botanic-garden landscape. name: Glasnevin Cemetery — O'Connell Circle and its sunken vault street — NIAH Registration 50130071
publisher: Department of Housing, Local Government and Heritage
specific_reference: NIAH Registration 50130071; official survey description, appraisal, rating and published Irish Grid coordinate 314741, 237184.
notes: NIAH rating: National. Multiple-bay circular vault and landscaped cemetery feature built c.1840. A circular street of family vaults is accessed by a sunken channel; the surface is laid out with funerary monuments in concentric circles. An original and nationally rated cemetery landscape designed by Patrick Byrne, conceived as the showpiece of the New Ground and formerly the temporary burial place of Daniel O'Connell before his reinterment beneath the round tower in 1869.
